_comment: Movement/feel constants EXTRACTED FROM REAL ALE RAM CAPTURE (room 1, frameskip=1, 60fps, sticky-actions off). Units are RAM-x/RAM-y, which on this game ≈ native 160x210 screen pixels (RAM-x≈screen-x, scale≈1.0; RAM-y is INVERTED — increases upward). Each value carries a confidence; LOW ones need a cleaner re-capture. Source CSVs in this folder.

walk_speed_px_per_frame.note: x changed +1/frame steadily while RIGHT held, -1/frame while LEFT. Symmetric. Clean.

jump.source: ram_walk_right.csv frames 120-140 (UPFIRE from rest on platform)

fitted_model.note: vertical speed steps down by 1 every ~3 frames; model as v0≈3.0 px/frame, g≈0.33 px/frame^2

fall.note: walking off the platform edge: -2/frame then accelerating to -3/frame (RAM-y down). Same ~0.33 gravity, terminal ~3-4.

climb_speed_px_per_frame.note: CONFIRMED on the central ladder (x=77): UP = +1/frame (RAM-y up), DOWN = -1/frame. Symmetric. Direction now agrees with the jump arc — the earlier contradiction was Joe falling OFF the ladder into the pit, not climbing.

player_size_px.note: width 12px from consecutive-frame diff (matches RAM-x walk stride). Height ~20 is the standard 2600 Panama Joe proportion; color-isolation was polluted by room-1 platforms, so re-measure if exactness matters.

y.note: PINNED. Fitted from 6 walk frames (RAM-y 192-233 mapped to pixel rows 89-122). Slope -0.85 confirms RAM-y increases upward AND that vertical RAM is ~1.18x finer than screen pixels (x is 1:1, y is not). Use uniform scale for a feel port; apply 0.85 vertically only for pixel-exact proportions.

derived_for_gym_game._comment: If the gym-gen canvas is authored at 2x native (320px wide), multiply RAM-unit speeds/sizes by 2. Drop into montezuma_revenge.js as constants. These are FEEL targets — tune the collision box until it matches.
derived_for_gym_game.note: player width / room width stays ~0.075 (12/160). Keep Joe ≥12px on source canvas per template.
